newsitem.title: THAILAND: Workers back at fire-hit Thai Sanyo plant.
newsitem.headline: Workers back at fire-hit Thai Sanyo plant.

text.p: Most employees of the fire-hit Thai Sanyo plant returned to work on Monday, six days after a fire which police and company officials said was set by dissatisfied colleagues following a row over bonuses.

More than 80 percent of Sanyo Universal Electric Plc's 3,500 employees reported back to duty at the firm's warehouse and seven-storey office building in the outskirts of Bangkok, the company officials said.
Police at the scene said they identified and arrested three more arson suspects, bringing the total held so far to 19 .
"We are hunting for more workers who were involved in the violence," a police spokesman said, adding they had identified the suspects from a videotape recording of the incident made by the company.
The arson drew strong protests from foreign investors and employer groups in the country. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh warned workers against a recurrence of such an incident in the future.
The Sanyo plant in Thailand is 30 percent owned by Sanyo Electric Co and a joint venture with local partners.

The plant, which makes refrigerators and other electrical appliances, would remain open for three days from Monday for employees to report back to work, company officials said. The plant would resume work on January 6 after the holidays.
The company said it was ready to pay year-end bonuses equal to four months pay, of which one month had already been paid. The workers had demanded 5.75 months in bonus.
It also denied it had intentionally burned down the warehouse and office to make insurance claims.
"We insured the company because we are a public company possessing assets and property worth more than 7.7 billion baht ($308 million)," a company statement said.
Police, insurance companies and Sanyo are working on the estimated cost of damage to the affected buildings.
A company source said it had initially estimated the cost of damage at about 300 million baht.
